topic: Mastering Limits: From Visual Intuition to Analytical Precision

sections.title: Intuitive Foundation: The Concept of 'Getting Closer'
lecture_lines: Limits describe behavior as x approaches a value.
The function doesn't need to exist there.
Consider f(x) equals x squared minus one over x minus one.
A robot vacuum approaches a charger point.
It converges without reaching the target.
animations: Animate a coordinate system fading in with white color (#FFFFFF).
Label the x and y axes with white color (#FFFFFF).
Represent the robot as a small circle in light green (#00FF00) moving toward the hole at x=1.
Show the robot stopping just before the hole, highlighting the limit at y=2 in bright yellow (#FFFF00).

sections.title: Formal Rigor: The Epsilon-Delta Definition
lecture_lines: Formal limits require epsilon and delta.
Epsilon defines the allowable error range.
Delta defines the input distance constraint.
animations: Draw a function f(x) in light blue (#00FFFF) on the screen.
Display an epsilon band around the limit value L in pink (#FFC0CB).
Indicate a corresponding delta interval on the x-axis in lime (#BFFF00).

sections.title: Computational Shortcut: L'Hôpital's Rule
lecture_lines: L'Hôpital's rule solves indeterminate limit forms.
Functions must be differentiable at the point.
Compare slopes to find the limit.
animations: Show an indeterminate form 0/0 in orange (#FFA500).
Represent two tangent lines at the point in light purple (#DDA0DD).
Visually shrink the ratio of the two functions to converge.
